retained_unadopted_draft.description_long: The Guardian's archive report, published Friday, October 25, 1968, described an arrangement under which News Ltd. was to take a 40 per cent stake in the News of the World after a takeover bid by Pergamon Press, the publishing group headed by Robert Maxwell, was defeated. The report said Rupert Murdoch, then chairman of News Ltd., was to become joint managing director with the newspaper's existing chairman, Sir William Carr. Its wording that the deal was unfolded the previous day places the report of the arrangement on October 24, although the archive item itself is dated October 25. The article describes a British newspaper ownership and management transaction; it does not report a Trump action or relationship. The frozen record's title and synopsis misidentify the newspaper titles and claim a bidding contest involving The Sun, while the accessible Guardian report concerns the News of the World. The linked TrumpFile page was reported in prior research as returning HTTP 202 without readable text. The supplied evidence therefore supports a narrow account of the 1968 transaction but gives no documented reason for placing it in a Trump-focused collection. Keep this copy as an exclusion review draft, not as a Trump-linked entry. The source says the stake and management changes were planned; it does not establish that they were completed.

source_fact_map.fact: The Guardian dated its archive report Friday, October 25, 1968.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: "News of World" in deal with Australia by Sandy McLachlan Friday 25 October 1968 guardian.co.uk Effective control of the "News of the World," Britain's biggest selling Sunday newspaper, is passing into the hands of an Australian company. In a deal unfolded yesterday to defeat the takeover bid by Pergamon Press, the publishing group headed by Robert Maxwell, MP, the Australian newspaper chain, News Ltd., is to take a 40 per cent stake in the "News of the World." This will be the largest single holding. The chairman of News Ltd., Mr Rupert Murdoch, is to become joint managing director of NoW, with the present chairman, Sir William Carr.
